text: At the harbor on Wednesday morning, I boarded the new Isolde-class ferry during its trial crossing and counted the rows of blue vinyl seats myself. Captain Mara Venn told me the vessel is built to carry 650 passengers, with space for 42 crew on busy routes. She said the ship, the Tern Wave, completed a 17-minute run between North Quay and Pelham Point under clear skies and light chop. I watched deckhands check the lifeboat stations, while a harbor inspector noted the widened gangway and extra stroller storage. By the time we docked, about 200 invited riders were already asking when the first public sailing would begin.
